Just another tech demo (like most VR games are) made in the early days of VR. Not worth £15. Not worth your time. But, as I said in one of my previous VR game reviews, this isn't the developer's fault. Why would a bunch of developers spend thousands of hours and hundreds of thousands of dollars developing AAA-quality games when the VR customer base is so low? On the other hand, I can't blame the customer base either. Why would someone buy bulky and expensive VR headsets and end up having to put up with subpar, crappy graphics due to technological limitations? VR still has a long way to go, and more Research and Development (R&D) is needed until we get to a point where the headsets will be affordable, high-quality, comfortable to wear, and deliver 4K quality graphics easily, just like modern monitors do. Until then, everything about VR is a paid tech demo.

I purchased this game back in 2018 when I first got my HTC Vive.  The problem is I wanted so many experiences when first jumping into VR, so I bought a bunch of games, but barely finished any.  Fast forward, and I'm now playing on the Valve Index and finally decided to jump back into playing more VR and giving this game a full go.  

All I can say is wow!  For a game that's pushing 8+ years old, it is fantastic.  The arcade gun play stays fun and satisfying the entire time.  I love all the different environments and moods.  The pace gets very tense at parts when a ton of enemies come at you at the same time, and it really sets you up to feel like a John Wick style monster killer.

I NEVER leave reviews, but had to give Phosphor Games their props.  I had a blast playing through this game end to end today!

Getting to and fighting off the cloverfield like monster was well worth it, having a huge mountain of a monster looming over you as you feebly attempt to fend it off with a pistol in VR is incredibly nerve racking but at the same time makes you feel like a badass

There are times when before you know it you are surrounded and a slight panic engulfs you as you clear your field of view only to still be being eaten by some thing. Good times. This game doesn't overstay its welcome either, not too long but not short either, 6-10 hrs to complete the campaign. It also has a survival mode. 

If you are looking for a VR shooter with great graphics and art then look no further. Enjoy The Brookhaven Experiment.

One of the first VR games I bought for the HTC vive, this horror shooter did not disappoint. This wave based zombie mutant shooter really got my adrenaline going as you stand in the middle of an arena and fight horde upon horde with nothing but a gun and a torch to help out. There's nothing more enjoyable than experiencing that primal fear of fighting to survive in such scary conditions. 

The game provides a number of guns to try using as well as a few different arenas in case the same one gets boring. On top of that, should you grow tired of shooting up the masses of mutants trying to kill you, then there is a campaign there ready to jump in at any time. With a bit more variation in enemies, weapons and arenas this game could have had 10/10 potential. However, in it's current state it is more than enjoyable
